TEXT_C:
The BNP’s 2010 manifesto casts itself as a defence of democracy, freedom, security and identity. It argues Britain faces an existential crisis from mass immigration, EU rule, multicultural “social engineering,” and Islamism, and pledges to put indigenous Britons first.

- Defence and foreign policy: End the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, oppose war with Iran, withdraw troops from Germany, renegotiate NATO to ensure independence, raise defence spending, and introduce a compulsory one‑year community service scheme. Adopt a neutral, interests‑first foreign policy, cease interference in the Middle East, and end foreign aid, reallocating funds to domestic needs.

- Immigration: Declare Britain a non‑immigration country; halt all further immigration; deport illegal immigrants and foreign criminals; review post‑1997 citizenship grants; expand voluntary resettlement; restore sovereign border control; and repeal the Race Relations Act and equalities bodies the BNP says enforce multiculturalism, while recognising law‑abiding settled minorities’ rights under a guaranteed British majority.

- EU: Immediate withdrawal to restore sovereignty, lawmaking and courts; end UK payments and EU regulation; rebuild global trade, especially with the Commonwealth.

- Counter‑jihad: Assert Islam is incompatible with secular democracy; ban the burka, ritual slaughter, and new mosques; stop immigration from Muslim countries; deport radical preachers and adherents; and address terrorism by ending mass immigration and adopting a neutral Middle East stance.

- Welfare and civil liberties: “Renationalise” welfare for Britons and contributors only; make the NHS serve British people, end “health tourism,” prioritise British staff, and cut bureaucracy; replace welfare with workfare; repeal ID cards, the Human Rights Act and ECHR jurisdiction; repeal laws restricting speech on race and religion; and reassert parliamentary sovereignty over courts.

- Constitution, media, culture: Devolve to revived counties; create an English parliament and a pan‑British parliament (inviting Ireland); reform the Lords with non‑party experts; introduce citizens’ initiative referenda; tighten postal voting and campaign rules; hold media criminally liable for knowing falsehoods and guarantee rights of reply; promote British history, traditions and saints’ days; protect pubs; and resist “alien” cultural influences.

- Crime: Remove political correctness from policing; restore deterrence with corporal punishment and capital punishment for specified crimes; strengthen householders’ self‑defence; impose hard labour, build a remote penal station for the most dangerous offenders, and ensure full sentences are served.

- Education: Restore traditional curricula, phonics, streaming, grammar schools, and competition; reinstate O‑ and A‑levels; prioritise STEM and vocational skills; free university for those completing community service.

- Transport and infrastructure: Reverse rail privatisation, invest in high‑speed maglev, reduce fuel taxes, charge foreign trucks, ease congestion by limiting immigration, and back new transport technologies.

- Agriculture, fisheries, energy: Support family farms; ban GM crops and non‑stunned slaughter; restore the 200‑mile exclusion zone; prioritise wave, hydrogen and especially nuclear and clean coal; oppose wind turbines and “carbon” levies; keep strategic energy in British hands.

- Housing: Empower councils to build for British citizens with local‑connection tests; abolish quangos; create an infrastructure bank; ease pressure by reversing immigration.

- Economy and industry: Cut spending on “global warming” schemes, immigration/asylum, EU, foreign aid, foreign wars, and quangos; raise the personal allowance to £12,500, restore a married allowance, lift IHT to £1m; curb multinationals’ tax avoidance and offshoring; vet foreign takeovers in the national interest; separate retail and investment banking; oppose privatising natural monopolies; deregulate SMEs; use selective tariffs against unfair imports; build local credit unions and explore local currencies.

- Pensions and IT: Raise the state pension to £150/week and link to earnings; limit reliefs and tighten eligibility to Britons/contributors; invest in technology universities; protect UK IT jobs; nationalise telecoms infrastructure to deliver universal 100 Mbps; strengthen data rights.

Conclusion: Democracy and freedoms are portrayed as imperilled by the EU and mass immigration; the BNP promises national renewal that puts British interests, security and identity first.

TEXT_F:
Labour’s 2010 manifesto sets out a post‑crisis programme for a future fair for all, built on active, reforming government. In the wake of the financial crash, Afghanistan and the expenses scandal, it rejects “business as usual,” pledging to secure the recovery, renew society, and restore trust in politics.

Economic strategy and fairness
- Secure the recovery by avoiding premature cuts, then more than halve the deficit by 2014 through growth, fair taxes and lower‑priority savings while protecting frontline spending on the NHS, schools, childcare and policing. Tough choices include public pay restraint, pension reform, efficiency savings and asset sales; tax fairness includes a 50p rate over £150k, a bank bonus tax, and a 1p NI rise while protecting the lowest paid.
- Reform finance to serve the real economy: tighter bank capital and pay rules, living wills, lending targets, more competition and a global levy; realise public stakes responsibly.
- Build a high‑tech, greener economy: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), a Green Investment Bank, HS2, universal broadband, ring‑fenced science, R&D incentives, patent box, and corporate governance reform (two‑thirds takeover threshold). Create one million skilled jobs, a regional growth fund, stronger SME support and apprenticeships.

Work, welfare and living standards
- End long‑term unemployment with guarantees: jobs or training for young people after six months; mandatory job offers after two years; extend tough‑but‑fair work capability tests with support for disabled people. Minimum Wage to rise with earnings; a £40/week Better Off in Work guarantee; Skills Accounts; clampdown on rogue employers.
- Help with housing and finance: stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers up to £250k (funded by 5% on £1m+ homes), more affordable homes, stronger repossession protections, a People’s Bank at the Post Office, universal access to basic bank accounts, and action on high‑cost credit.

Education and children
- Increase frontline spending on Sure Start, childcare, schools and 16–19 learning; expand free nursery places. A legally backed 3Rs guarantee with one‑to‑one tuition for pupils falling behind; personal tutors in secondary; stronger leadership through accredited school groups, academies and co‑ops; parental power to trigger leadership change. Raise participation to 18, expand advanced apprenticeships and widen HE access.

NHS and care
- Protect NHS budgets, reinvest up to £20bn efficiencies, and shift to prevention and personalisation. Legal guarantees: 18‑week treatment or funded private care; one‑week cancer test results; mid‑life health checks; choice of qualified providers; extended GP access; talking therapies; one‑to‑one cancer nursing; more care at home.
- Create a National Care Service: free home care for the greatest needs from 2011, a cap on residential costs after two years, national standards, and expanded individual budgets. Support families with a Father’s Month, a Toddler Tax Credit, extended flexible working and an end to default retirement at 65. Re‑link the Basic State Pension to earnings from 2012 and auto‑enrol millions into pensions.

Safety, communities, immigration and culture
- Maintain police/PCSO numbers; neighbourhood teams visible and accountable; faster action on anti‑social behaviour with a right to injunctions; expand Community Payback; use CCTV and DNA to tackle serious crime. Control immigration through the points‑based system, earned citizenship and English proficiency, aligning flows with economic need.
- Back thriving communities: protect post offices and pubs; empower supporters’ trusts in football; uphold BBC independence; deliver a golden Olympic legacy; support arts and free museums.

Green transition
- About 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 via renewables, new nuclear and clean coal/CCS; 400,000 green jobs; “pay as you save” home upgrades, smart meters, warmer homes for pensioners; move towards zero waste; protect and connect habitats, maintain the Green Belt and expand woodlands; a Supermarket Ombudsman for fair food chains.

Democratic renewal and global role
- Clean up politics and empower citizens: AV referendum, staged election of a reformed second chamber, fixed‑term parliaments, a lobbyists’ register, recall for misconduct, open data and stronger local government through Total Place.
- Support troops and veterans; a Strategic Defence Review; maintain the nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament. Lead in a reformed EU, legislate 0.7% aid from 2013, and advance climate, security and development goals.

Contrasting a pessimistic, backward‑looking Conservatism, Labour offers an optimistic, practical, progressive programme to secure recovery and build a fairer, stronger Britain.
